minutes.headline: Voters debated expanding the water district to reach contaminated 110 Birch Street land; outcome unclear from captions
minutes.summary: This was the Lunenburg Water District's annual meeting, covering routine budget, borrowing and equipment articles (Articles 2-6), an election-bylaw amendment (Article 7), and a contested article to expand the district's boundary to serve 110 Birch Street, a parcel with a long history of DEP contamination cases, where extensive public comment split between residents fearing spread of contamination and those citing fire protection and well-water reliability. The election-of-officers article was deferred to 4pm balloting, and results (a Commissioner race and the Moderator race) were read out when the meeting reconvened; the district's board also announced a water quality survey for resident input.

what_happened.line: Voters took up expanding the water district to reach 110 Birch Street, a parcel with a history of DEP contamination cases, but the vote's outcome was not audible on the recording.
Voters adopted the FY2027 operations and maintenance budget as amended, for the amount as heard, after a resident objected to vague open-ended wording.
Voters first declined to pass over election-bylaw changes, then amended and adopted them, including new recount procedures.
Voters authorized the treasurer to borrow against anticipated FY2027 revenue if resident bills go unpaid on time.
The district's board announced a resident water-quality survey after the contamination debate.

why_it_matters: Whether the district's boundary reaches 110 Birch Street affects who can hook into town water, who would owe betterment or tie-in fees, and whether a subdivision or other development becomes feasible on land with a contamination history.
The adopted FY2027 budget sets what the water district spends on operations, maintenance and elected officers' pay, funded from district income rather than the town's general tax levy.
The bylaw changes reset how recounts and vote observation work in future water district elections, which residents raised after past recount requests were denied.
